newsitem.title: UK: Asprey says sales ahead of last year.
newsitem.headline: Asprey says sales ahead of last year.

text.p: Asprey, the UK jeweller, owned by Prince Jefri Bolkiah of Brunei, said progress in the half year since its interim results has been good.

Last week, the luxury retailer, known as jeweller to Britain's Royal Family, took a 17 million stg provision for slow moving stock and a pretax loss of 21.7 million for the year up from a pretax loss of 9.82 million previously.
The group made trading profits from continuing operations of 7.67 million. Turnover rose 20 percent to 212.9 million stg.
"Progress in the half year since these results has been good, sales are over 15 percent ahead of last year and trading profit is ahead of the group's business plan," said chief executive Ian Dahl.

He was responding to an article in the Financial Times newspaper, which focused on the company's 17 million pound provision. "It is important to put the article and the results into perspective, the group made a trading profit last year of 7.7 million pounds.

"However, the board decided to address the key strategic issues by including significant charges in the year's results, the largest element 17 million pounds was related to stock and involved review of all stock in all departments in all divisions," said Dahl in a statement.
"Any stock which was old, inapprorporate and slow selling in the current market was provided against," he said.
Dahl said retail sales margins had strengthened and heavily discounted sales, generating no profits, eliminated.
"Clearance of old stock is on target, with a quarter of the provision stock now cleared.. Programmes to clear the stock in all the group's retail divisions are progressing well," he said.
